title: Econ Sentinel Bridge: unified profile-to-rollout playbook for batching, caching, and quantization
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Goal: build an operational playbook (Econ Sentinel Bridge) that converts route-level telemetry into safe, automated rollout artifacts for batching, KV-prefetching, and quantization profiles. This reduces unit token cost while bounding tail-latency and quality regressions. The playbook covers: 1) data collection and canonical profiling, 2) candidate policy generation (batch sizes, TTLs, quant profiles), 3) risk scoring and canary gating, 4) rollout automation + rollback guards, and 5) post-rollout validation and cost attribution. Output: a reproducible pipeline + console integrations (Runbook template, per-route cost/latency deltas, and a verification checklist).
acceptance_criteria: Canonical profiler runs nightly and produces per-route histograms (latency, seq-length, prefix-hit-rate)
Automated candidate generator suggests at least 2 viable batching + TTL + quant configurations per high-volume route
Canary gate executes safety checks (latency SLO, top-20 prompt eval set quality thresholds) and will auto-rollback on regression
Integration with Console: per-route preview of estimated cost delta and 95th latency delta before rollout
Field trial on 3 pilot routes shows >=18% reduction in token-unit cost with <5% tail-latency increase and no quality regressions on eval set
progress_updates: 2025-01-14: Kickoff with Eng (serving/runtime), Research (quant team), and DevRel. Aligned on scope: only routes with >50 r/s and stable model pin will be considered for automated rollouts.
2025-01-21: Data schema decided — use existing telemetry stream (kafka: route-profiles-v2). Eng to deliver proto by 2025-01-28. Action: ENG to add cache-hit and prefix-kv metrics to span payload.

2025-01-28: Engineering PR opened implementing profiler ingestion (GH: redwood/realtime#2364). Initial runs show heavy skew in sequence-length for chat-routing routes; batching yields limited wins for multi-turn flows.
2025-01-31: Decision: split candidate generation into two phases — conservative (small batch, high TTL) and aggressive (larger batch, quant-8 mix). Product requested safety-first for Q1 pilots.

2025-02-03: Design review with Console team — added UI requirement to preview estimated cost delta and to mark routes as 'pilot-eligible'. Design feedback: add an explicit override and manual rollback button. Next: produce PRD and rollout runbook draft.

2025-02-03: Blocker logged: need access to historical top-100 prompts per route for quality evals. Solutions: 1) request customer opt-in retention flag for pilots, or 2) synthesize prompts using anonymized shells. Security team to advise on option 1 by 2025-02-07.
metrics: Target token cost reduction: 15-25% across pilot cohort
Max acceptable 95th latency increase: +10% absolute or 50ms, whichever smaller
Quality regression threshold: <1% drop on route-specific eval set (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim) or manual vet signoff
Adoption KPI: 30% of enterprise routes tagged pilot-eligible within 8 weeks
